questions.note: Hallux longest, toe 2 a little shorter; hallux ~31 mm wide (678 px at 21.7 px/mm in hr.front, 611 px at 20.0 in hr.plantar), toe 2 ~15.5 mm (740 px at 47.6): in tolerance. Shaping is generic: one wrinkle stamp on IP and PIP, a box-sided hallux from below with no toe-base sulcus; on toe 2 a plantar seam, a knife-cut DIP crease, a finger-long distal segment; a shelf web.

Hallux plate ~19.5 mm wide (849 px at 43.5 in hr.hallux), toe 2's ~10 mm (476 px at 47.6, at the low edge); free edge ~0.85 mm thick (76 px at 89), trimmed straight, no floating or sunk plate. But no hallux lunula; the plate washes near-white like acrylic, sits in a crisp gutter with an S-kink, its free edge an opaque plastic slab; toe 2's is a manicured fingernail.

In scope, nothing: no EHL relief over the first MTP or along the hallux's proximal phalanx and no extensor slip to toe 2 in hr.front or hr.medial; the only dorsal relief is a scar-like raised arc. A lean 40-year-old shows the EHL as a soft cord catching the rim light. Veins and the saphenous lie outside this scope.

SSS is believable: the shadow sides of both toes stay dark, no glow. Micro-relief is wrong in kind: plantar ridges are uniform diagonal stripes, the dorsal crackle glints like crumpled cellophane, the web recess and the pulp under the free edge go smooth. The declared first-pass shader adds an oily sheen; I did not mark the score down for tone or gloss.

defects.what: The hallux plate washes to an even near-white sheen over its upper half, with two broad soft highlight blobs in the full view: polished acrylic, not keratin, and no pink bed reads through it.
defects.fix: Keratin has a modest sheen broken by fine longitudinal ridges; raise the plate's roughness and let the bed's pink show through a translucent plate, paler only toward the free edge.

defects.what: The plantar ridges are straight parallel stripes at one diagonal angle over the hallux pad, toe 2's pads and the ball alike, running through the IP crease: corduroy or brushed metal at native size.
defects.fix: Friction ridges form a whorl or loop on each toe pad, curved transverse arcs on the proximal pads and the ball, and stop or bend at every flexion crease.

defects.what: The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP carry the same stamp: three or four long, evenly spaced, parallel glossy grooves spanning the joint, which in hr.medial dent the dorsal outline like bellows.
defects.fix: Knuckle skin has short, uneven, broken transverse creases of differing depth and length with a fine cross-hatch between, more of them on toe 2's PIP than on the hallux IP; the outline stays nearly smooth.

defects.what: From below the hallux is a straight-sided rounded box that grows straight out of the ball: no sulcus at the toe base, only a faint IP crease, no separate oval pulp pad.
defects.fix: A real hallux has a deep plantar crease where it leaves the ball, a clear IP flexion crease, a slimmer proximal segment and an oval pulp pad bulging past it.

defects.what: Along its lateral edge the hallux plate sits in a crisp, deep gutter with a bright exposed rim, the plate's side wall showing, like a press-on tile; the medial edge is a thin incised line.
defects.fix: A lateral nail fold is a soft roll of skin that rises slightly over the plate edge and hides it; the groove is a shadowed tuck, never a sharp rim.

defects.what: The free edge is a uniform-width opaque grey-cream slab from corner to corner, smooth as plastic, its rounded corner ending flush on the lateral fold with no gap or shadow beneath.
defects.fix: A clipped toenail edge is whitish-yellow and slightly translucent, its cut face layered and a little uneven, with a shadowed hairline of grime under it and the corners standing just clear of the fold.

defects.what: A thin raised glossy arc crosses the first MTP dorsum and notches the dorsal outline in hr.medial; a podiatrist reads a healed bunionectomy scar.
defects.fix: At rest the skin over the first MTP is smooth or carries a few soft, short transverse wrinkles; never a single raised ridge.

defects.what: The hallux hairs are straight, even strokes splayed in chevrons and crossing pairs, their directions spread over some 70 degrees, like scratches rather than hair lying in one flow toward the tip.
defects.fix: Hallux hairs emerge singly, curve gently and lie flat distally and slightly laterally within about 20 degrees of each other, tapering to fine tips, 5–8 mm long.

defects.what: The 1–2 web ends in a ruler-straight horizontal margin with a square corner at toe 2, a shelf rather than a web; the same line shows in hr.front.
defects.fix: The web margin is a soft U, deepest midway between the toes, its free edge a rounded fold that blends into each toe's side.

defects.what: Toe 2's nail is a neat tombstone with parallel sides, outlined by a crisp raised rim on three sides and a constant-width cream edge: a manicured fingernail rather than a lesser toenail.
defects.fix: A second toenail is a small convex shield, slightly narrower at the root, its sides half-tucked under soft puffy lateral folds, its free edge a little uneven.

defects.what: Toe 2's distal segment reads finger-long: about 8 mm (390 px at 47.6 px/mm, before foreshortening) of bare skin between the DIP crease and the nail fold, where a toe's nail starts 2–4 mm past the crease.
defects.fix: Move the proximal nail fold back toward the DIP crease, or the crease forward, so the nail covers most of the short distal phalanx (11 mm bone, 10 mm nail).

defects.what: From below a straight crisp seam with a light ridge crosses toe 2 and its outline steps in at it on both sides, so the toe's end reads as a cap fitted on, like the old toes 3–4.
defects.fix: The plantar PIP crease is a soft, gently curved fold with the pads bulging either side; the outline dips smoothly into it and never steps.

defects.what: No lunula reads on the hallux in any view: the plate is one even pale pink from the proximal fold to the free edge apart from specular blobs, where the spec asks for a visible 3.5 mm crescent.
defects.fix: Add a dull, slightly paler half-moon with a soft convex distal border, centred and partly under the proximal fold, about 3.5 mm deep.

defects.what: The plate's medial edge has a sharp S-kink: the fold bulges over the mid-plate, then the plate flares out to the free-edge corner, so the outline looks traced around a bump.
defects.fix: The visible plate edge follows the lateral fold in one smooth, gently convex line from the proximal corner to where the free edge leaves the groove.

defects.what: Toe 2's DIP crease is one long continuous groove across more than half the toe, a knife cut rather than two or three short, soft, broken creases.
defects.fix: Two or three short, shallow, interrupted transverse creases over the DIP, set in slightly looser skin.

defects.what: No EHL cord rises over the first MTP onto the hallux's proximal phalanx and no extensor slip runs to toe 2: the dorsum is smooth where a lean 40-year-old shows soft ridges catching the light.
defects.fix: Model the EHL as 0.5–1.5 mm relief along the hallux's dorsal midline to the distal phalanx base, and a finer extensor slip onto toe 2.

defects.what: In highlights the dorsal micro-relief is a crumpled-cellophane crackle of sharp, glinting facets, the same on knuckle, shaft and web; the glints already show in hr.toe2.
defects.fix: Toe skin shows a soft polygonal network of fine shallow grooves 0.25–0.6 mm across, rounded not faceted, breaking the highlight into a soft sheen, with follicle pits.

defects.what: Below the hallux free edge the pulp and hyponychium are blurred and featureless while the side wall beside them carries a crisp crackle: detail sharp in one place, soft in the next.
defects.fix: Carry the fine skin texture and the first friction ridges across the distal pulp up to the hyponychium at the same scale as the side wall.

defects.what: The shadowed web recess is a smooth, blotchy smear with no micro-relief, like denoiser smudge, so the web skin goes waxy.
defects.fix: Keep the skin network and creases in the recess, dimmed by the shadow but not smoothed away.

defects.what: In clay a hairline pinch runs down the junction of the web and toe 2's medial wall instead of a soft concave fillet.
defects.fix: Blend the web's dorsal surface into toe 2's side with a rounded fillet a few millimetres wide.

ranked: [D1] The hallux nail, the focus of most views, reads as polished acrylic: broad soft highlights wash the plate near-white and no pink bed shows through. Keratin has a smaller sheen broken by fine ridges, over a pink bed.

[D2] From below the ridges are uniform diagonal stripes over the hallux pad, toe 2 and the ball, crossing the creases: corduroy at native size. Real pads carry a whorl or loop, the ball curved arcs, all broken at the creases.

[D3] The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wear one stamp of three or four long, even, glossy grooves that dent the outline in profile like bellows; real knuckles have short, broken, uneven creases and a near-smooth outline.
[D4] From below the hallux is a straight-sided box growing straight out of the ball: no sulcus at the toe base, a faint IP crease, no separate oval pulp pad.
[D5] Laterally the hallux plate sits in a crisp, deep gutter with a bright exposed rim, its side wall showing: a press-on tile. A real lateral fold is a soft roll of skin tucked over the plate edge.

[D6] The free edge is a uniform opaque grey-cream slab, plastic-smooth, its corners ending flush on the fold; a clipped edge is whitish, slightly translucent and uneven, with a shadowed hairline of grime beneath.
[D7] A thin raised glossy arc over the first MTP dorsum notches the outline in profile and reads as a healed bunionectomy scar.
[D8] The hallux hairs are straight, even strokes splayed in chevrons and crossing pairs, like scratches; real hairs curve gently and lie flat toward the tip in one flow. Toe 2 has a single tiny tick.
[D9] The 1–2 web ends in a ruler-straight horizontal shelf with a square corner at toe 2; a web margin is a soft U, deepest midway, its edge a rounded fold.
[D10] Toe 2's nail is a neat tombstone with parallel sides, a crisp rim on three sides and a constant cream edge: a manicured fingernail, not a lesser toenail half-hidden by puffy folds.
[D11] Toe 2's distal segment reads finger-long, about 8 mm of bare skin between the DIP crease and the nail fold; on a second toe the nail starts just past the crease.
[D12] From below a crisp straight seam crosses toe 2 and the outline steps in at it, the end reading as a cap fitted on, like the old toes 3–4.
[D13] No lunula reads on the hallux: the plate is one even pale pink up to the fold, where most men's big toenails show a dull, paler half-moon partly under it.
[D14] The hallux plate's medial edge kinks in an S, the fold bulging over the mid-plate and the plate flaring at the corner, as if traced around a bump.
[D15] Toe 2's DIP crease is one long continuous knife cut instead of two or three short, soft, broken creases.
[D16] No EHL cord over the first MTP onto the hallux and no extensor slip to toe 2: the dorsum is smooth where a lean man shows soft ridges catching the light.

The declared first-pass skin shader gives every dorsal surface an oily sheen and one tone from knuckle to tip; it exaggerates the glints of the grooves and crackle and keeps the toes reading young and clean.
[D17] In highlights the dorsal micro-relief glitters like crumpled cellophane, sharp facets alike on knuckle, shaft and web.
[D18] Below the hallux free edge the pulp is smooth and blurred while the side wall beside it is crisply crackled: detail sharp in one place and soft in the next.
[D19] The shadowed web recess is a featureless smear, so the web skin goes waxy where it should stay finely textured.
From below, toe 2's tip ends in a small cluster of dark crumpled creases at its rim, reading as pinched skin rather than a smooth pulp dome meeting the nail.
[D20] In clay a hairline pinch runs down the junction of the web and toe 2's medial wall instead of a soft concave fillet.
